speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me exactly what antibiotic you took and for what illness, and when did your symptoms start?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count with Differential, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, and ESR/CRP.

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your urgency, but we must identify the cause to ensure your safety. While you wait for the blood work results, did the itchy rash appear specifically on the areas where you had a previous allergic reaction, or is it new to your body?

REQUEST TEST: Antibody_Panels (including Diphtheria, Tetanus, and Pertussis).
REQUEST IMAGES: [Full_body_skin_examination, Joint_exam]

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results showing normal readings suggest your body isn't currently fighting an active infection or suffering from severe inflammation. Did the rash appear immediately after taking the antibiotic, and did you experience any swelling of your lips, tongue, or difficulty breathing at that time?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diagnosed with acute sinusitis one week ago, no known history of adverse drug reactions, immunizations up to date. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of acute sinusitis treated with antibiotics, combined with a new itchy rash and joint pain, were the symptoms that started immediately after your last dose?

REQUEST TEST: Specific_IgE_An Antibody_Panels for Penicillin, Amoxicillin, and Cephalosporins.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Hypersensitivity Reaction (likely amoxicillin-induced morbilliform exanthem with arthralgia).
